summary: Benchmark Qwen3.8-27B as a local Pass D dossier generator against the frontier baseline
description:
Paired A/B: can a local model (Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL on llama.cpp, 3090) replace claude-opus-4-8 for Pass D L1 span summarization?

WHY IT MIGHT WORK. The rubric names the characteristic frontier failure: 'fluent well-formed prose that silently imports outside knowledge... the model knows a great deal about these texts and will write it confidently and correctly. Correct is not the standard. Supported by the input is.' A 27B knows less about these texts, so it has less to leak. GROUND and LEAK are structurally easier for a weaker model. The capability actually needed is instruction-following, not knowledge.

WHY IT MIGHT NOT. COVERAGE (strict source order, proportion) and FORMAT are capability limits a smaller model is worse at. l1-v3 exists because frontier models failed COVERAGE/GROUND three times.

DESIGN (settled, do not re-derive):
- Compare ONLY within prompt_version. L1 baseline is fragmented: l1-v2 = 834 accepted, l1-v3 = 36 accepted. Comparing local-v3 against frontier-v2 measures the template revision, not the model.
- Free paired set = the 36 spans with accepted frontier l1-v3 rows: iamblichus-on-the-mysteries 22, egyptian-heaven-and-hell 11, apocryphon-of-john 3. span_target is provider-independent by design, so span ids survive a provider switch — that is what makes pairing possible.
- Those 3 works contain NO sayings/logia collection, the genre where l1-v3's source-order rule is most likely to break. Baseline needs extending.
- Measure the failure-code distribution and template_defect rate, NOT accept rate alone. Hypothesis: GROUND/LEAK down, COVERAGE/FORMAT up.

SCOPE: Phase 1, L1 only. Explicitly NOT in scope: the fold/map-reduce path (folds exist only for L2 under input_budget>0 and that code has never run) and the structured fields (context/key_figures/key_terms/reading_notes, where FORMAT retries against MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 will cost most). Both are follow-ups gated on Phase 1 passing. A good L1 result does NOT imply the pipeline is ready.

CONSTRAINTS: guru main is protected, PR flow only. Work on a guru.db snapshot from scripts/backup_db.sh, never the live DB. Nothing is auto-promoted; the apply gate stays with the owner. Est. ~1-2h GPU for 36 spans plus judge calls.

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content: Workflow note: this plan uses the FEATURE BRANCH method (feat/c8-local-dossier-bench) rather than the CLI's todo/<parent-id> convention. 'todo work <child> --branch feat/c8-local-dossier-bench' keeps the state machine correct, but 'todo close' emits an advisory warning ('HEAD is on feat/..., expected todo/8c67ee44') and proceeds anyway. The warning is expected, not a failure. Do not switch branches to satisfy it.

resolution.note: Closed: not yet, provider stays claude-code. Full findings, root cause, and what would need to change: docs/dossiers/decisions/local-model-benchmark.md. Kept: run-qwen-generate.sh, run-qwen-judge.sh, and the SEED/REASONING_BUDGET/EXTRA_ARGS reproducibility fix in serve-llama.sh — all three independent of the go/no-go outcome. Not kept: the investigation's raw data, intermediate per-run docs, and three throwaway analysis scripts, which cluttered docs/dossiers/ without being operational reference; removed before merge, preserved in branch history.
